{"allowed_envs":["PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_ADMIN_TOKEN","PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONTROL_URL","PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONTROL_TOKEN","DSTACK_ROOT_PUBLIC_KEY","CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN","CERTBOT_EMAIL","NODE_EXPORTER_USER","NODE_EXPORTER_PASSWORD_HASH","PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_PULL_TOKEN","PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_PREFIX_HASH_SECRET","PRIVATEMODE_API_KEY"],"docker_compose_file":"# dstack / Phala deployment manifest for the private-ai-gateway stack via the launcher.
#
# The launcher image is the measured trust-root: pin it by @sha256 digest (the
# digest + this file are hashed into the TDX quote). The launcher clones+builds
# the gateway from source at boot; the attestation verifier is
# the gateway's vendored confidential_verifier package, so it needs no separate pin.
#
# The gateway's source pin + static config are inlined as compose `configs:`
# (measured into the attestation): the launcher clones the pin and the gateway
# reads the config from mounted files. Secret values are supplied as dstack
# ENCRYPTED SECRETS and referenced as ${VAR} so dstack injects them — only the
# variable names appear in this public file, never the values.

services:
  # TLS-terminating ingress: requests Let's Encrypt certs via Cloudflare DNS-01 for a
  # KMS-derived TLS key, registers under the dstack gateway domain, and reverse-proxies
  # inbound 443 to the launcher's gateway on :8086. Pin by @sha256 digest like the
  # launcher. DETERMINISTIC_TLS_KEY survives renewals from 2.7 on
  # (Dstack-TEE/dstack-examples#132); published on GHCR only.
  dstack-ingress:
    image: ghcr.io/dstack-tee/dstack-ingress:2.8@sha256:60e682449534715a2f2e5b72326ca4229209c8e26c931c6f34d27e02200ac086
    restart: unless-stopped
    # The ingress is an L4 TCP proxy: every client connection maps 1:1 to a
    # backend connection to the gateway, so it holds 2 fds per live connection.
    # haproxy has no `ulimit-n` in its config; it derives an fd need from MAXCONN
    # and raises its OWN soft nofile from the container hard limit. Pin the hard
    # limit here (like `launcher`) so MAXCONN is never silently capped by whatever
    # the docker daemon default happens to be. 65536 comfortably covers
    # MAXCONN 16384 (~33k fds) with headroom.
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      # --- public config: literals, measured into the attestation ---
      DNS_PROVIDER: cloudflare
      GATEWAY_DOMAIN: gateway.${DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN}
      # One TLS key per domain, derived from the dstack KMS (path tls/<domain>), so every
      # replica serves the same key and renewals never change it. The gateway reads the
      # served certificate's SPKI only at startup, so a key that changed on renewal made
      # the attested SPKI stale. The key changes only with a new app ID or KMS.
      DETERMINISTIC_TLS_KEY: "true"
      # No CAA record. With one ACME account per replica, each replica replaced the
      # others' accounturi CAA and renewals failed. Clients pin the attested SPKI, so
      # CAA is defense in depth. The existing CAA records must be deleted once by hand:
      # this flag only stops writing them.
      SET_CAA: "false"
      # Concurrent-connection ceiling. The image default is 4096; under real
      # streaming load the ingress sat pinned at that ceiling ~84% of the time
      # (avg ~3720 concurrent), so once a burst pushed past 4096 haproxy stopped
      # accepting and clients saw a hang. Streaming LLM traffic keeps thousands of
      # long-lived connections open at once, so give a 4x headroom. Must stay well
      # under the nofile hard limit above (2 fds/conn in TCP mode).
      MAXCONN: "16384"
      # Idle (no-data) timeout, reset on any byte in either direction. The image
      # default is 86400s (24h): a client that stops reading, or an upstream that
      # goes silent, keeps its slot for a full day, which is how slots leaked
      # toward the ceiling. 1800s reaps a genuinely idle/stalled connection while
      # never touching a stream that is still flowing (even a slow one). NOTE:
      # this is the one value to confirm against the longest legitimate silent
      # gap a request can have — e.g. a reasoning model that thinks >30 min before
      # its first token would be cut. Raise if such requests are expected.
      TIMEOUT_CLIENT: 1800s
      TIMEOUT_SERVER: 1800s
      # Multi-domain TLS. The ingress is an L4 (TCP) proxy: it terminates TLS for
      # each hostname and forwards the DECRYPTED stream untouched, so the client's
      # original HTTP Host survives. The gateway uses that Host to pick the
      # matching downstream_tls_binding. All public hostnames route by SNI to the
      # same gateway listener (compose service name, not localhost). tee.redpill.ai
      # and inference.phala.com are the TEE-only domains (see `tee_only_domains`
      # below).
      DOMAINS: |
        tee.redpill.ai
        inference.phala.com
        api.redpill.ai
      ROUTING_MAP: |
        tee.redpill.ai=launcher:8086
        inference.phala.com=launcher:8086
        api.redpill.ai=launcher:8086
      # --- secrets: values come from dstack Encrypted Secrets (never commit values) ---
      # NOTE: this single Cloudflare token must have DNS-edit (and CAA) rights on
      # BOTH the redpill.ai and phala.com zones, or cert issuance for one fails.
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}
      CERTBOT_EMAIL: ${CERTBOT_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      - /var/run/dstack.sock:/var/run/dstack.sock
      - /var/run/tappd.sock:/var/run/tappd.sock
      - cert-data:/etc/letsencrypt
      # Per-domain leaf certs (cert-<domain>.pem) the gateway reads to bind SPKI.
      - evidences:/evidences

  launcher:
    image: ghcr.io/redpill-ai/private-ai-launcher@sha256:c083ff9e6a5ddf10f6c9e9bb1f74cc618deebecfea5208b563c574399db4637c
    restart: always
    # The gateway opens many fds (inbound conns, per-upstream pools, control-plane
    # + verifier calls). Docker's default nofile (often 1024) is far too low: under
    # load it hit EMFILE ("Too many open files"), which killed the gateway's accept
    # loop. Raise the limit well above peak concurrency.
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    # supervisord streams the gateway logs to the container stdout; cap the
    # runtime log on disk so it can't grow unbounded (~500MB total, rotated).
    # The gateway writes no per-request lines — startup, verification, and its
    # own errors only — so the volume is low.
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "100m"
        max-file: "5"
    # no host port: traffic enters via dstack-ingress (443) and reaches the
    # gateway over the compose network as http://launcher:8086.
    expose:
      - "8086"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/dstack.sock:/var/run/dstack.sock   # only the gateway uses this
      - pal-cache:/var/lib/pag/cache                 # cargo/uv build cache (speeds reboots)
      - pal-state:/var/lib/pag/state                 # mutable upstreams.json + sessions.jsonl
      - evidences:/evidences:ro                      # ingress-minted per-domain leaf certs (cert-<domain>.pem)
      - privatemode-manifests:/run/privatemode-manifests:ro
    # Static gateway config + upstream seed are mounted from the `configs:` block
    # at the bottom (measured into the attestation). The source pin is passed via
    # `environment:` instead (see below).
    # `docker compose up` does NOT recreate the container when only a `configs:`
    # content changes, so the old file stays mounted. Bump this label whenever
    # gateway-config / gateway-upstreams change to force a recreate.
    labels:
      private-ai-gateway.config-rev: "4"
    configs:
      - source: gateway-config
        target: /etc/private-ai-gateway/gateway.config.json
      - source: gateway-upstreams
        target: /etc/private-ai-gateway/upstreams.seed.json
    secrets:
      - source: privatemode-api-key
        target: privatemode-api-key
    depends_on:
      - privatemode-proxy
    environment:
      # The gateway reads its whole policy from this mounted static config file
      # (see `configs:` above); CONFIG_PATH is the only gateway-facing env var.
      - PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH=/etc/private-ai-gateway/gateway.config.json
      # Tracing filter. The gateway does not log requests; failures are
      # accounted for in the control plane's usage pipeline.
      - RUST_LOG=info
      # Gateway source pin. These literals are measured into the attestation, and
      # because they live in `environment:` (part of Compose's config-hash) a
      # COMMIT_SHA bump forces a container recreate on `phala deploy` — so the new
      # pin actually takes effect. (A `configs:`-file pin would not: Compose ignores
      # config content when deciding to recreate, so the change would never apply.)
      # entrypoint.sh writes /etc/git-launcher/gateway.conf from these, and the
      # gateway reads that file as its attested source provenance.
      - PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_REPO_URL=https://github.com/Dstack-TEE/private-ai-gateway.git
      - PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_REPO_COMMIT=22d08e24129804c72b0bfce6f547636992a3f559
      # NEAR AI verification posts TDX quotes to the dstack-verifier sidecar below;
      # reach it by compose service name (localhost would be the launcher itself).
      - DSTACK_VERIFIER_URL=http://dstack-verifier:8080
      # --- secrets: values come from dstack Encrypted Secrets (never commit values) ---
      # Control-plane credentials. The gateway's in-process middleware reads these
      # from the `middleware` config section below (rendered from the same secrets).
      - PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONTROL_URL=${PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONTROL_URL}
      - PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONTROL_TOKEN=${PRIVATE_AI_GATEWAY_CONTROL_TOKEN}

  # Official Privatemode proxy, co-deployed on the private Compose network.
  privatemode-proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/edgelesssys/privatemode/privatemode-proxy@sha256:3cd4da0ee6ceee91ca84dde4e3e3f0e94e8b354d7c1d46987e4331a5c2f8bcff
    command:
      - --workspace
      - /var/lib/privatemode
      - --port
      - "8080"
      - --api-key
      - "@/run/secrets/privatemode-api-key"
      - --api-key-fallback=always
      - --disable-prompt-cache=false
      - --nvidia-ocsp-allow-unknown=false
      - --nvidia-ocsp-revoked-grace-period=0
    tmpfs:
      - /var/lib/privatemode:mode=0700
    volumes:
      - privatemode-manifests:/var/lib/privatemode/manifests
    secrets:
      - source: privatemode-api-key
        target: privatemode-api-key
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "50m"
        max-file: "5"

  # TDX quote verifier for the NEAR AI path (reproduces ACPI/boot measurements via
  # QEMU). The gateway reaches it at http://dstack-verifier:8080 (DSTACK_VERIFIER_URL).
  dstack-verifier:
    image: ghcr.io/dstack-tee/dstack-verifier:0.6.1@sha256:9f2c07a94efd3d8a1a89268e5faa35e91e3cb345b9c4ab859c86d35142f4f788
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "50m"
        max-file: "5"

  # Host-metrics exporter for observing this CVM (CPU/mem/disk/net/fd). Inside a
  # CVM the container's /, /proc, /sys ARE the guest's, so node-exporter reports
  # the CVM's own state. Pinned by @sha256 like the other images (measured into

      - '--path.procfs=/host/proc'
      - '--path.sysfs=/host/sys'

    volumes:

    ports:
      - "9100:9100"
    logging:

      options:

  cert-data:   # Let's Encrypt certs/keys persisted for dstack-ingress
  evidences:   # ingress attestation evidence + per-domain leaf certs, shared read-only with the gateway

","features":["kms","tproxy-net"],"gateway_enabled":true,"kms_enabled":true,"local_key_provider_enabled":false,"manifest_version":2,"name":"","no_instance_id":false,"pre_launch_script":"#!/bin/bash
echo "----------------------------------------------"
echo "Running Phala Cloud Pre-Launch Script v0.0.15"
echo "----------------------------------------------"
set -e

# Function: notify host

notify_host() {
    if command -v dstack-util >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        dstack-util notify-host -e "$1" -d "$2"
    else
        tdxctl notify-host -e "$1" -d "$2"
    fi
}

notify_host_hoot_info() {
    notify_host "boot.progress" "$1"
}

notify_host_hoot_error() {
    notify_host "boot.error" "$1"
}

# Function: Perform Docker cleanup
perform_cleanup() {
    echo "Pruning unused images"
    docker image prune -af
    echo "Pruning unused volumes"
    docker volume prune -f
    notify_host_hoot_info "docker cleanup completed"
}

# Function: Check Docker login status without exposing credentials
check_docker_login() {
    local registry="$1"

    # When registry is specified, check auth entry for that registry in Docker config
    if [[ -n "$registry" ]]; then
        local docker_config_path="${DOCKER_CONFIG:-$HOME/.docker}/config.json"
        if [[ -f "$docker_config_path" ]] && grep -q "$registry" "$docker_config_path"; then
            return 0
        else
            return 1
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback check when no explicit registry is provided
    if docker info 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Username"; then
        return 0
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main logic starts here
echo "Starting login process..."

# Check if Docker credentials exist
if [[ -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" && -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" ]]; then
    echo "Docker credentials found"
    DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET="${DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"
    echo "Target Docker registry: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"

    # Check if already logged in
    if check_docker_login "$DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY"; then
        echo "Already logged in to Docker registry: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
    else
        echo "Logging in to Docker registry: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
        # Login without exposing password in process list
        if [[ -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY" ]]; then
            echo "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" | docker login -u "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" --password-stdin "$DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY"
        else
            echo "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" | docker login -u "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" --password-stdin
        fi

        if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "Docker login successful: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
        else
            echo "Docker login failed: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
            notify_host_hoot_error "docker login failed"
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
# Check if AWS ECR credentials exist
elif [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" && -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" && -n "$DSTACK_AWS_REGION" && -n "$DSTACK_AWS_ECR_REGISTRY" ]]; then
    echo "AWS ECR credentials found"

    # Check if AWS CLI is installed
    if [ ! -f "./aws/dist/aws" ]; then
        notify_host_hoot_info "awscli not installed, installing..."
        echo "AWS CLI not installed, installing..."
        curl "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64-2.24.14.zip" -o "awscliv2.zip"
        echo "6ff031a26df7daebbfa3ccddc9af1450 awscliv2.zip" | md5sum -c
        if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "MD5 checksum failed"
            notify_host_hoot_error "awscli install failed"
            exit 1
        fi
        unzip awscliv2.zip &> /dev/null
    else
        echo "AWS CLI is already installed: ./aws/dist/aws"
    fi

    # Set AWS credentials as environment variables
    export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$DSTACK_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
    export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$DSTACK_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
    export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="$DSTACK_AWS_REGION"

    # Set session token if provided (for temporary credentials)
    if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]]; then
        echo "AWS session token found, using temporary credentials"
        export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN"
    fi

    # Test AWS credentials before attempting ECR login
    echo "Testing AWS credentials..."
    if ! ./aws/dist/aws sts get-caller-identity &> /dev/null; then
        echo "AWS credentials test failed"
        # For session token credentials, this might be expected if they're expired
        # Log warning but don't fail startup
        if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]]; then
            echo "Warning: AWS temporary credentials may have expired, continuing startup"
            notify_host_hoot_info "AWS temporary credentials may have expired"
        else
            echo "AWS credentials test failed"
            notify_host_hoot_error "Invalid AWS credentials"
            exit 1
        fi
    else
        echo "Logging in to AWS ECR..."
        ./aws/dist/aws ecr get-login-password --region $DSTACK_AWS_REGION | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$DSTACK_AWS_ECR_REGISTRY"
        if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "AWS ECR login successful"
            notify_host_hoot_info "AWS ECR login successful"
        else
            echo "AWS ECR login failed"
            # For session token credentials, don't fail startup if login fails
            if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]]; then
                echo "Warning: AWS ECR login failed with temporary credentials, continuing startup"
                notify_host_hoot_info "AWS ECR login failed with temporary credentials"
            else
                notify_host_hoot_error "AWS ECR login failed"
                exit 1
            fi
        fi
    fi
fi

perform_cleanup

#
# GHCR image pull access verification (pure HTTP, no docker daemon)
#
if [[ "$DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET" == "ghcr.io" && -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" && -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" ]]; then
    COMPOSE_IMAGES=$(grep 'image:' /dstack/docker-compose.yaml 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '"'"'" || true)
    for img in $COMPOSE_IMAGES; do
        [[ "$img" != ghcr.io/* ]] && continue
        repo="${img#ghcr.io/}"; repo="${repo%%:*}"
        tag="${img##*:}"; [[ "$tag" == "$img" || "$tag" == "$repo" ]] && tag="latest"
        echo "Verifying GHCR pull access: $img"
        token=$(curl -sf -u "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME:$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD"             "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:${repo}:pull" | jq -r '.token // empty' || true)
        if [[ -z "$token" ]]; then
            echo "ERROR: GHCR token exchange failed for $img"
            notify_host_hoot_error "GHCR token exchange failed: $img"
            exit 1
        fi
        http_code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $token"             -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json,application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json"             "https://ghcr.io/v2/${repo}/manifests/${tag}")
        if [[ "$http_code" != "200" ]]; then
            echo "ERROR: GHCR pull access denied for $img (HTTP $http_code)"
            notify_host_hoot_error "GHCR pull access denied: $img (HTTP $http_code)"
            exit 1
        fi
        echo "GHCR pull access OK: $img"
    done
fi

#
# Pull latest images from docker-compose.yaml so existing CVMs pick up new tags.
# Pull is fail-soft: short-lived tokens may expire between login and pull, but
# falling back to already-cached images is preferable to blocking boot.
#
echo "Images before pull:"
docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}} ({{.CreatedSince}})'

echo "Pulling latest images from /dstack/docker-compose.yaml..."
if docker compose -f /dstack/docker-compose.yaml pull; then
    echo "docker compose pull completed"
    notify_host_hoot_info "docker compose pull completed"
else
    echo "WARNING: docker compose pull failed; continuing with existing images"
    notify_host_hoot_info "docker compose pull failed; using existing images"
fi

echo "Images after pull:"
docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}} ({{.CreatedSince}})'

#
# Set root password.
#
echo "Setting root password.."

# Check if password files are writable
PASSWD_WRITABLE=true
if [ ! -w /etc/passwd ]; then
    echo "Warning: /etc/passwd is read-only"
    PASSWD_WRITABLE=false
fi

    if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS" ]]; then

        if [[ $(jq 'has("ssh_authorized_keys")' /dstack/user_config 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]; then
